A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Alberta Wells Dataset work. All 28 pages of each, including Appendices A–E, support comparison; relocated figures, tables, and appendix material can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation and detection benchmarks, NIR ablations, and active-only versus all-well training results in Tables 4–8.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports DETR benchmark results and further qualitative predictions.

M1.justification: The dataset construction, clustering-based splitting algorithm, and annotation procedures are retained. DETR is introduced as an evaluated baseline, not as a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Alberta imagery covering active, suspended, and abandoned wells for binary segmentation and detection. Table 9 retains 188,688 patches and 213,447 wells. Additional illustrative cases do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds DETR with a ResNet50 backbone alongside the retained RetinaNet, Faster R-CNN, FCOS, and SSD Lite baselines. Qualitative detection examples also switch from FCOS to DETR; the quantitative segmentation comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added DETR experiment specifies a ResNet50 backbone and batch size 64 under the stated 120-epoch detection training protocol. Qualitative U-Net examples switch from EfficientNetB6 to ResNet50. Existing quantitative splits, metrics, preprocessing, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: The NIR, well-type, and backbone comparisons are retained. v3 revises the prediction examples and adds dedicated failure cases in Figure 4 and further predictions in Appendix Figure 11, extending qualitative error inspection without adding a quantitative robustness study.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same ± reporting practice, without specifying repeat counts, seeds, or what the uncertainty values represent. The added DETR row follows this existing format; no new statistical estimation or testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds DETR results, including mAP50 of 15.22 ± 0.28 and mAP50:95 of 38.45 ± 0.32, the highest reported values in those columns. RetinaNet's mAP50:95 changes from 0.72 ± 1.12 to 0.63 ± 1.12. Other quantitative benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged, while qualitative predictions are revised and expanded.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1's mathematical substance and the metric explanations are retained. Neither version adds theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations; differences in mathematical typesetting do not establish revised reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the first-large-scale-benchmark contribution, the segmentation/detection framing, and the claim that existing models show promise but leave substantial challenges. DETR does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 attributes DETR's performance to global contextual cues and adds limitations concerning dense regions, weak well signatures, and insufficient spectral cues in Section 6. It removes v2's speculation about surpassing human performance. Existing geographic and missing-label limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 promises future code availability, whereas v3's new Software and Data section reports benchmarking code as available. Appendix E.6 corrects its dataset access link to Zenodo, and DETR settings are documented. Some appendix passages still describe future code release, so actual availability is not established consistently by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds Carion et al. (2020) for DETR and removes background references to Sykas et al. (2022), Teng et al. (2023), and Chen et al. (2017). The prior well-dataset comparison and overall novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. v3 condenses Section 5.3 and background discussion, adds access and hosting headings, and updates funding, affiliation, and citation presentation. The abstract's change from medium- to high-resolution terminology leaves the stated 3-meter imagery unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to an ICML two-column layout, substantially resizing and repositioning tables and Algorithm 1. The quality-control flowchart moves to the appendix, Tables 6 and 7 exchange order, and prediction grids are redesigned and expanded with Figures 4 and 11. Existing appendix illustration grids are also shortened. Algorithm 1 acquires a malformed comparison glyph.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves benchmark usefulness by adding a transformer detector and makes failure behavior more explicit through additional examples and limitations. Access documentation also improves. These benefits are limited by incomplete integration: Section 5.2 retains highest-score statements for earlier detectors that conflict with the new DETR row, and code-release wording remains inconsistent. The retained dataset and principal experiments prevent this from being a substantial overall advance.
